results.evidence: Second independent source found for the west col, the col between Cashmere's West Peak and the main peak, where the west ridge scramble begins. (1) The peak list publishes the West Peak's key saddle at 47.55891,-120.85206 (7,977 ft LiDAR). (2) The SummitPost Cashmere Mountain page has a 2013 Garmin GPS track (872 points, recorded elevations) in its archived GPX download. That track passes 3 m from this point, at 7,979 ft, and the page's text routes both variations through 'the col between the west peak and the main peak'. (3) A third, independent 2020 CalTopo route line ('Cashmere via Eightmile') passes 14 m from it, with vertices on either side (47.55891,-120.85225 and 47.55893,-120.85155). The row's own track passes 4 m from it, but that track is corroboration only and is not counted as a source. USGS 3DEP reads 7,976 ft at the point (confirmation only). The stored 'Base of west ridge' pin (47.5575,-120.842) reads 7,308 ft and sits 771 m east of the col on the far side of the summit, so it is moved. Height: the peak database gives the West Peak's key col as 8,000 ft, a second page restates 8,000 ft, and the peak list's 7,977 ft LiDAR value agrees within 23 ft. The stored 6,800 is therefore set to 8,000 on both elev keys. Name unchanged, since the scramble starts at the col. Not changed: distMi 5.2 on this pin, which is short for a col beyond Little Lake Caroline; nothing states a figure for it.

results.evidence: The stored waypoint 5 'Walrus (Clark) Glacier rope-up / crevasse zone' (48.04725024,-120.96234512, elev 7,000) is not at the rope-up. A USGS 3DEP profile along the ridge from the summit to Pt 8373 shows it sits at that ridge's low point (about 7,950-8,000 ft): the '8000 ft col' reached after the glacier, just below the summit. Two independent sources place the rope-up bench on Clark's eastern arm, about 1.9 km east of the pin. (1) A public 2016 CalTopo map, 'Clark Mountain Walrus Glacier', has a marker titled '6700' at 48.05036669713597,-120.93634128570551, on the arm north-west of Boulder Pass. (2) A 2019 Gaia GPS track (3,010 points with times and elevations) passes 93 m from that marker at 6,764 ft. Its trip report says the party dropped about 150 ft from the pass, crossed the basin north-west, climbed about 500 ft to the top of the ridge, and 'reached the glacier ... We roped up'. The track shows a 27-minute stop at the top of that ridge (48.049346,-120.937811), 157 m from the marker. Two text accounts with no coordinates fit the same place: one says the party descended from Boulder Pass, climbed to a '6700-foot bench on Clark's eastern arm' and roped up there; the other gives '6760' roped up' on the way from a 6,100 ft camp. The two coordinate sources are independent: the CalTopo map was last updated 2016-07-03, three years before the track. The pin is moved to the CalTopo marker's published coordinate. Elevation: the CalTopo label '6700' and the first text account's '6700-foot bench' both state 6,700, so elev 7,000 becomes 6,700. The pin has no elevFt key, so none is added. The row's own track passes 195 m from the new point and 48 m from the track's rope-up stop. CAVEAT for the owner: the CalTopo marker names the spot only by its height, and the track's rope-up is read from the report's narrative plus a 27-minute stop. Also, this pin's own 'directions' text (traverse east under Peak 7242, then back west to the glacier toe) and its note ('east of Boulder Pass') describe the approach differently. That text is NOT edited here.

results.evidence: No published coordinate or public GPS track was found for the ~5,400 ft cliff band / bypass gully or the ~6,100 ft point where the route regains the crest. Searched: OpenStreetMap (only the summit node 47.6167948,-121.2715514; no path on the ridge), CalTopo and Gaia public maps (none for this peak), SummitPost (its page and GPX are not archived), peak databases (archived pages expose no track data), and NWHikers (the 2006 thread is neither archived nor readable without a browser check). The detailed 2019 report gives only heights ('cliff wall straight ahead at 5400', veer left into a small gully, rising traverse into the upper basin, back to the ridge at 6100'). Its 'GPS track: available' link leads to a photo album, not a track. The row has no track to test against. Pins 2-4 stay as they are: they are imprecise, but not demonstrably off this east-side bypass line, and no published coordinate exists to move them to.
